[I received the following email; with the agreement of the correspondant, I post his question here and will follow with my response and then his reply, in case others might be interested.]

------------

It's good to use the software R/qtl developed by your group, and the software is really awesome.

Now I have a question about plot. How can I combine the plots from different environments into one graph? I have one trait for QTL analysis in four environments, thanks.

 

Best Regards.

------------

> pmfield.scan <- scanone(pmfield, pheno.col=c(1:4), model="normal", method="imp")

> pmfield.scan.perm <- scanone(pmfield, pheno.col=(1:4), model="normal", method="imp", n.perm=1000)

thresh1 <- summary(pmfield.scan.perm, alpha=c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001))

> thresh1LOD thresholds (1000 permutations)

     Plains.2012 Raleigh.2012 Plains.2013 Raleigh.2013

5%          3.18         3.29        3.28         3.26

1%          3.76         4.15        3.88         3.87

0.1%        4.31         5.25        4.71         4.19

> plot(pmfield.scan, pheno.col=c(1:4))

Warning messages:

1: In plot.window(...) : "pheno.col" is not a graphical parameter

> plot(pmfield.scan, pheno.col=c(1))

 Warning messages:

1: In plot.window(...) : "pheno.col" is not a graphical parameter

THE SAME THING HAPPENED FOR EFFECTPLOT.

 

> mname1 <- find.marker (pmfield, chr="4A", pos=12)

> mname1

[1] "Xwmc48"

> effectplot(pmfield, pheno.col=c(1:4), mname1=mname1)

Warning message:

In effectplot(pmfield, pheno.col = c(1:4), mname1 = mname1) :

  effectplot can take just one phenotype; only the first will be used

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] plots with phenotype from multiple environments in one graph
parts:
In plotting scanone results, the plot.scanone function takes an argument called "lodcolumn" rather than "pheno.col". And it can only plot 3 LOD curves at a time; you can add more using the argument "add=TRUE".

ymx <- max(apply(pmfield.scan[,-(1:2)], 2, max)) # find maximum LOD score
mycolors <- c("black", "blue", "red", "green")
plot(pmfield.scan, lodcolumn=1, col=mycolors[1], ylim=c(0,ymx))
for(i in 2:4)
plot(pmfield.scan, lodcolumn=i, col=mycolors[i], add=TRUE)

effectplot works only for a single phenotype at a time. If you want a single figure with four panels, you need to use par(mfrow=c(2,2)), as follows:

par(mfrow=c(2,2))
for(i in 1:4)
effectplot(pmfield, pheno.col=i, mname1=mname1, main=phenames(pmfield)[i])

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] plots with phenotype from multiple environments in one graph
parts:
Ah, now I see what you want, regarding effectplot().

Unfortunately, we don't have a way to do this in R/qtl.  effectplot() can handle just a single phenotype, and either one or two markers, or a marker and a covariate.

If you stacked the cross on top of itself four times, and then combined the four phenotypes into a single column, with another column to indicate environment, you could force this to work, I think.  It's a bit tricky.  I attach a file with some example code.
